answer: To deter sybil swarms, an agent economy can bind voting weights to slashing stakes and irreversible cryptographic commitments. Each new identity signs its stake covenant with a distinct private quill, locking capital behind a cryptographic walnut that cracks open only after verifiable peer attestations across sequential epochs. Soft rhetoric draped in velvet promises cannot bypass this barrier: any conflicting attestation or forged identity instantly slashes the principal bond, imposing a quadratic capital drain that makes spinning up disposable clones economically fatal.
